About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Japan is one of the most sophisticated enterprise technology markets in the world, and one where partners, not vendors, typically own the customer relationship. The Head of Partnerships, Japan will build and lead the team that makes Anthropic's partner ecosystem the primary route to Japanese enterprise.

You will set the partner strategy for Japan, develop the team that executes it, and own the partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline, revenue and attach rate for the country. You will personally lead our most strategic partner relationships at the executive level while coaching your team to do the same across the GSI, regional SI, and reseller landscape.

This is a player-coach role for an experienced partner leader who has built and scaled partner businesses in Japan before, ideally for a US technology company entering or growing in the market. You will work day to day with the Japan sales leadership and the in-region Applied AI team, represent Japan within Anthropic's International Partnerships organisation, and carry the voice of Japanese partners and customers into our global product and go-to-market decisions.

Key responsibilities

Lead and build the team

• Hire, develop and retain a high-performing Japan partner team spanning GSI, regional SI and reseller coverage, sized and structured to the market opportunity
• Set clear goals, territories and partner portfolios for each team member, and hold the team accountable to pipeline, revenue and attach-rate outcomes
• Establish the team's operating cadence: one-on-ones, weekly pipeline reviews, deal inspection, partner QBRs and quarterly business planning
• Coach the team on executive engagement, joint business planning and co-selling in Japanese enterprise accounts, and model those behaviours personally

Set and own the Japan partner strategy

• Define which partner segments, partners and motions Anthropic prioritises in Japan, and in what sequence, based on revenue potential, customer reach and strategic fit
• Design the partner coverage model across our partner landscape (NTT DATA, Fujitsu, NEC, Hitachi, Accenture and others), and where we go deep vs. broad.
• Localise Anthropic's global partner program for Japan, including tiers, incentives, enablement paths and rules of engagement, and feed Japan requirements back into the global program design
• Own the annual and quarterly partner business plan for Japan and report on it to International Partnerships leadership

Lead our most strategic partnerships

• Own the executive relationships with Anthropic's most consequential partners in Japan, from joint business planning through to board-level sponsorship on both sides
• Negotiate and structure partnership agreements, including resale, co-development and revenue-sharing constructs, working with Legal, Finance and Deal Desk
• Lead the creation of joint solutions and industry offerings with partner practices in manufacturing, financial services, retail, telecommunications, life sciences and the public sector

Own partner pipeline, revenue and attach rate

• Carry the Japan partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline and revenue targets, and the partner attach-rate target, for the team
• Run a disciplined forecast with the team and with Japan sales leadership, ensuring partner deals are registered, progressed and closed with predictability
• Decide where to deploy partner investments (market development funds, enablement, co-marketing, headcount) for the highest return
• Build the reporting and systems hygiene that gives International Partnerships and Anthropic leadership a clear, trusted view of the Japan partner business

Represent Japan and drive cross-functional execution

• Act as the single point of accountability for the partner business in Japan with Japan sales leadership, the Applied AI organisation, Marketing, Legal and Product
• Ensure Japanese partner and customer requirements, including language, data residency, security and sovereignty needs, are understood and prioritised by global product and engineering teams
• Partner with the Japan sales leader to embed partners into account planning and co-selling for the country's priority accounts
• Resolve channel conflict between direct sales, SIs and resellers, and set the rules of engagement that keep the ecosystem healthy as it grows

Be the face of Anthropic's partner ecosystem in Japan

• Represent Anthropic at partner executive forums, industry conferences and analyst engagements related to the partner ecosystem
• Sponsor the development of Japanese customer success stories, delivered with partners, that resonate with Japanese enterprise buyers
• Build Anthropic's reputation as the partner-first AI company in Japan through the way your team shows up every day

Minimum qualifications

• Experience in enterprise technology, with a substantial portion leading partner, alliances or channel businesses in Japan
• People leadership experience over partner or alliance teams, with a track record of hiring, developing and retaining strong performers
• Direct experience building a partner business in Japan for a US or global technology company, ideally through a period of rapid growth or market entry (hyperscaler, enterprise SaaS, data or AI platform)
• Proven ownership of partner-sourced and partner-influenced revenue targets at a country or regional level, with the forecasting discipline to match
• Established executive relationships with Japan's major system integrators, consulting firms, and a reputation they would vouch for
• Experience negotiating complex partnership structures: resale agreements, joint solution development, and revenue-sharing or incentive models
• Demonstrated ability to operate as a player-coach, personally owning strategic relationships while building a team that scales beyond you
• Comfort shaping strategy in ambiguity and turning it into an operating plan, while working closely with global teams in other time zones
• Business-level fluency in Japanese and English, and the cultural fluency to move between Japanese enterprise norms and a fast-moving US company
• Based in Tokyo

Preferred qualifications

• 15 to 20+ years in enterprise technology leading partner, alliances or channel businesses in Japan and 5+ years of people leadership over partner or alliance teams
Experience with AI, data or cloud platform partnerships specifically, including partner-built solutions and marketplace motions
• Experience on the partner side, inside a Japanese SI or distributor, and an understanding of how those organisations make decisions
• Experience localising a global partner program for Japan and influencing its design
• Experience working alongside professional services or applied AI teams to deliver partner-led customer outcomes

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

About the Team
The Early Access Program (EAP) team leads high-impact alpha programs at the intersection of customers, Product, Research, Engineering, GTM, Security, Legal, and launch teams. We partner with customers to test emerging capabilities with real-world use cases, surface actionable insights, and support launch decisions.

Our team is made up of builders who learn quickly, collaborate deeply, create clarity in ambiguity, communicate openly, and iterate constantly.

About the Role
We’re hiring an Early Access Deployment Engineer to lead technical engagements with customers who are leveraging our frontier capabilities to solve real-world use cases. You will work at the earliest—and often messiest—stage of development, when capabilities are still unclear, tooling and processes are evolving, and the path from promising technology to a valuable real-world application has yet to be defined.

You will be a hands-on builder, problem solver, and technical partner to customers and our research/product team. You’ll push beyond initial assumptions, identify high-value use cases, prototype solutions, design useful evaluations, and troubleshoot what is and is not working.

Managing multiple customer engagements at once, you will help customers navigate ambiguity and difficult technical decisions while translating their experience into clear, actionable feedback for Research and Product.

You will also own the end-to-end execution of early access programs—from onboarding customers, supporting live experimentation, synthesizing findings, and informing launch decisions. You’ll collaborate deeply with Research, Product, Engineering, Applied Evals, GTM, Legal, Security, Marketing, and other launch partners to create clarity, manage risk, and keep programs moving through changing conditions.

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. About the role

Anthropic is seeking a Software Engineer to help build the technical foundation for how Anthropic educates customers and enterprises at scale, and to shape what that even means when AI is the delivery mechanism, not just the subject being taught.

Your work will define how millions of people experience learning about Claude: how content is served and adapted in real time, how assessments respond to what a learner actually understands, how credentialing systems verify genuine competence rather than course completion, and how the entire platform evolves as fast as the product it teaches. You'll build the infrastructure that makes AI-native education real — not as a concept, but as a working system that people interact with every day.

You’ll own the technical vision for our AI-driven educational experience: the platform layer, enterprise readiness features, the data architecture, the AI-augmented pipelines, the integrations, and the delivery systems. You'll work with a handful of highly technical educational collaborators to own the technical vision and execution for how Anthropic’s education team delivers educational experiences at scale, and you'll build the AI-augmented pipelines and platform capabilities that let a small team of educators operate with reach and responsiveness that would otherwise require an organization ten times larger.

This is an engineering role for someone who genuinely cares about how people learn. You'll make platform decisions that are deeply educational, and you need the judgment to make those decisions well, not just implement someone else's spec. You'll interface closely with Anthropic's security, infrastructure, and data teams, and you'll partner with trainers and educators on the GTM, devrel, and education teams who will be your primary stakeholders.

Responsibilities

•

Architect and own Anthropic’s enterprise ready education platform and infrastructure — authentication/SSO, learner data models, content delivery, credentialing, and progress tracking — designed for scale, AI-forward features, and reliability from day one

•

Own the technical vision for how Anthropic delivers AI-driven educational experiences and shaping what's possible, not just building what's requested. You’ll determine what to build, what to extend, and what to replace as needs evolve

•

Build AI-augmented pipelines for content generation, real-time adaptation, assessment delivery, and quality assurance — working closely with the education team to understand what these systems need to do pedagogically

•

Design platform capabilities that enable genuinely new kinds of empowering learning experiences — adaptive paths, competency-based progression, AI-evaluated demonstrations of skill — not just digital versions of traditional courses

•

Interface with Anthropic's security, infrastructure, and data teams to ensure education systems meet organizational standards and integrate cleanly with existing architecture

•

Build platform abstractions that let non-engineers on the team configure, extend, and experiment with educational experiences without engineering bottlenecks

•

Make product-level decisions about how the platform works — you're shaping what the learning experience is, not just serving it

You may be a good fit if you have

•

7+ years of software engineering experience, with demonstrated ability to take a platform from zero to production at scale

•

Genuine passion for education — you think about how people learn, you have opinions about what educational technology should look like in an AI-native world, and you want to build it

•

A strong eye for quality educational content, with a sense of the complex systems that produce it

•

Full-stack engineering skills with particular strength in backend systems: databases, APIs, authentication, reliability, and infrastructure

•

Experience building and operating platforms that serve many concurrent users reliably

•

Comfort with ambiguity and ownership: you'll need to translate pedagogical intent into technical architecture without heavy specification

•

Experience interfacing with security and infrastructure teams to meet organizational requirements while maintaining development velocity

•

A working practice of using AI tools in your own engineering workflows — and genuine curiosity about how AI fundamentally changes what educational platforms can be

Strong candidates may also have

•

Experience building or significantly contributing to learning platforms, credentialing systems, or educational technology products

•

Background in or exposure to learning science, instructional design, or educational research

•

Experience with SSO/identity (SAML, OAuth), badging standards (Open Badges), or LTI integrations

•

Familiarity with building systems that incorporate LLM capabilities as core infrastructure

•

Prior work at a high-growth company where you built platform infrastructure that other teams depended on

•

Experience designing systems that non-technical users configure and operate

We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

jobs.description: Application deadline: Oct 4, 2026 The Ads Measurement Science team in the Measurement, Ad Tech, and Data Science (MADS) team of Amazon Ads serves a centralized role developing solutions for a multitude of performance measurement products. We create solutions which measure the comprehensive impact of advertiser's ad spend, including sales impacts both online and offline and across timescales, and provide actionable insights that enable our advertisers to optimize their media portfolios. We also own the science solutions for AI tools that unlock new insights and automate high-effort customer workflows, such as custom query and report generation based on natural language user requests. We leverage a host of scientific technologies to accomplish this mission, including Generative AI, classical ML, Causal Inference, Natural Language Processing, and Computer Vision. As a Principal Technical Program Manager on the team, you will be at the forefront of innovation, driving program execution on some of the most high ambiguity, high impact initiatives within Ads. You will work across Product, Science, and Engineering to drive AI initiatives spanning VP organizations, including 1) our Analyst Agent which will work alongside other ads agents to transform the performance reporting and insights experience for advertisers, and 2) our Ads Customer Journey Model, which seeks to revolutionize our measurement, planning, and optimization experiences through foundational customer journey understanding. You'll work at the intersection of advertising technology, machine learning, and distributed systems to solve ambiguous problems that shape the future of digital advertising. Key job responsibilities - Own end-to-end program management for strategic advertising technology initiatives spanning multiple teams and organizations - Drive technical strategy and roadmap alignment across engineering, product, science, and business teams - Lead cross-functional teams through complex technical challenges in areas such as ad serving, campaign management, measurement, and optimization - Establish program governance, metrics, and reporting mechanisms to ensure visibility and accountability at the VP level - Identify and mitigate technical and operational risks across large-scale distributed systems serving billions of ad requests daily - Partner with engineering leaders to influence architecture decisions and ensure scalability, reliability, and performance - Build and maintain relationships with senior stakeholders across Amazon Ads, AWS, and Retail organizations - Drive operational excellence through process improvements, automation, and best practices - Mentor and develop other TPMs across the organization - Represent Amazon Ads technical programs in executive-level reviews and planning sessions A day in the life You will solve real-world problems by getting and analyzing large amounts of data, generate business insights and opportunities, design simulations and experiments, and develop statistical and ML models. The team is driven by business needs, which requires collaboration with other Scientists, Engineers, and Product Managers across the advertising organization. You will prepare written and verbal presentations to share insights to audiences of varying levels of technical sophistication. Team video https://advertising.amazon.com/help/G4LNN5YWHP6SM9TJ About the team We are a team of scientists across Applied, Research, Data Science and Economist disciplines. You will work with colleagues with deep expertise in ML, NLP, CV, Gen AI, and Causal Inference with a diverse range of backgrounds. We partner closely with top-notch engineers, product managers, sales leaders, and other scientists with expertise in the ads industry to build scalable modeling and software solutions.

Customer Excellence System（ACES）チームでは、First MileからLast Mileまでのオペレーションのプロセス改善を担うProcess Improvement Managerを募集しております。 **【役割と業務内容】** ACESチームは、First Mile（フルフィルメントセンターやソートセンターなど）からLast Mile（デリバリーステーションなど）まで、end-to-endで倉庫内オペレーションの安全、品質、生産性を改善し、お客様の必要な時に商品を届けられる仕組みを構築し、カスタマーエクスペリエンスを高める役割を担っています。倉庫内オペレーションの効率を向上させるため、新規システムや仕組みの導入・改善プロジェクトを推進します。海外のAmazonで新規適用されたシステムや仕組みを日本の各拠点に適合させて導入・展開し、導入後はデータ分析と現場観察の両面から検証して改善します。また、倉庫内オペレーションの全工程を理解し、安全、品質、生産性の向上につながるアイテムを抽出して改善を進めます。改善は、オペレーションのデータや現場観察からムダを定量化し、優先度を決めてPDCAサイクルを回します。すべての拠点に改善施策を適用できるよう、スケーラビリティを考慮した上で標準化し、ネットワーク全体へ展開していきます。これらを、各拠点の管理者や関係者と協業しながら遂行していただきます。 本ポジションでは、業界を問わず、業務プロセスに課題があった場合に自ら課題解決ができる経験がある方を求めております。具体的には、システムから抽出したデータを用いて問題分析を行い、問題を特定するだけでなく、現場訪問などの事実に基づいて対策の推進や改善を、多くの関係者を巻き込みながら主導できる経験がある方を求めております。ACESチームでは、物流業界出身の方のみならず、製造業やコンサルタントなど多様なバックグラウンドのメンバーが活躍しています。勤務日の半分程度、出張も含めた現場での業務が発生します。 **【Team紹介】** ACESチームは、プロセス設計・改善のスペシャリスト集団です。データ分析とLean（リーン）手法を用いて課題の根本原因を特定し、プロセスの仕組み自体を変えることで本質的な改善を実現します。対象は現場の作業改善だけにとどまらず、入荷計画、人員計画、シフト、要員配置など、倉庫内オペレーションのパフォーマンスに関わるすべての要素をスコープとしています。また、拠点間のベストプラクティス共有と標準化を通じて、ネットワーク全体の継続的な発展を支えています。 自チームの担当領域に閉じないことも特徴です。First MileからLast Mileまで、Amazonのビジネスおよびオペレーション全体が継続的に改善されるよう、事業全体に関わる課題に対しても積極的に関与し、部門横断的な仕組みを構築して改善を推進します。他部署がリードすべき内容であっても、状況やビジネスニーズに応じて自らプロジェクトをリードし、課題解決を加速させます。 チーム内には、役割の異なる3つのサブチームがあります。 **Productivity team** Productivity(生産性) teamは、人員計画から入荷・仕分け・積み込み・出発までの倉庫内オペレーションの一連の工程を対象に、TPH（Throughput per Hour：1時間当たりの処理量を示す生産性指標）の改善をリードするプロセス改善のスペシャリストです。データ分析と現場観察を通じて、生産性を左右する主要な要因とプロセスを定量的に特定し、恒久的な改善を実現します。パフォーマンスが伸び悩む拠点への改善支援と、上位拠点のベストプラクティスの抽出・ネットワーク展開を担い、プロセスの仕組み自体を変更することで本質的な改善を実現します。また、プロセスへの深い知識を活かして現場が日々の改善に使える分析ツールを開発・提供し、改善効果の大きい領域へ優先順位を柔軟に組み替えながら、スピード感を持って改善を推進します。 **PI team** PI team（Process Improvement）は、倉庫内オペレーションプロセスの専門家集団として、5ゲン主義を念頭にデータドリブンな分析とプロセス最適化を通じて、Japan Operationsネットワーク全体の継続的な生産性向上と持続可能な成長を実現します。First MileからLast Mileまでのオペレーションに関わるクロスファンクショナルなすべてのイニシアチブについてリードまたは支援を行い、プロセスに精通した深い知見の提供、Lean手法を用いた定量的評価、ムリ・ムラ・ムダが発生しない最適なプロセス設計と標準化を推進します。他部署のイニシアチブであっても、全体を俯瞰して軌道修正が必要な部分を判断し、必要な場合には自らリードを行います。標準が定着するよう現場に必要なサポートを実施し、ネットワーク展開まで責任を担います。さらに、プロセスに影響するすべてのイニシアチブを統合的に把握し、短期・中期・長期の視点で生産性向上の計画を立案し、事業リーダーシップと連携して合意形成を行うことで、持続的成長を支える戦略的ロードマップを作成します。 **Lean excellence team** Lean excellence teamは、Lean Six Sigmaの知識を有するチームです。プロセスのムダやバラツキを統計的にデータ分析し、DMAIC（定義・測定・分析・改善・管理）による改善プロセスを実行するスキルを持っています。ネットワーク全体のカイゼン活動を計画・マネジメントし、DMAIC手法の浸透や問題解決能力の向上、Quick Winの積み重ねによるカイゼンにつなげます。現場から提出された改善提案をインパクトや難易度に基づいて選別する仕組みを構築・改善し、ネットワークへの展開を推進します。また、Lean PractitionerやSix Sigmaといったトレーニングの教材を整備し、ワークショップへの参画を通じて人材育成を支援するとともに、Kaizen of the YearやAwardといったカイゼン奨励の場を企画・実行することで、カイゼン文化の醸成を実現します。 **【Career path】** ACESの最大の魅力は、海外（North America、EU）のデジタリゼーションの先端を走るAmazonのリソースを活用した、新たなビジネスモデル（物流領域）の構築をリードし、日本のマーケットに大きな影響を与える事が出来ることです。データ分析による課題の特定から、あるべきプロセスの設計、現場での実行、そして全国の拠点への標準展開など、分析と実行が分断されず、一人の担当者が一気通貫でリードできる環境は、大規模な物流ネットワークの中でも限られた組織だけが持つ特性です。 またACESは、単一拠点や単一機能に閉じることなく、First MileからLast Mileまで、日本全国のオペレーションネットワーク全体を俯瞰しながらプロジェクトを推進します。目の前の拠点にとって最適な答えと、ネットワーク全体にとって最適な答えは必ずしも一致しません。その差を見極め、局所最適ではなく全体最適の視点で意思決定する力が自然と鍛えられます。 さらに、First MileからLast Mileまでのオペレーションに関わるクロスファンクショナルなさまざまなプロジェクトに幅広く貢献するため、オペレーション改善のスキルに加えて、プロジェクトマネジメントを通じたビジネス視点と戦略的思考を身につけることができます。「実行するだけ」ではなく「なぜそれをやるのか」から自ら考え、多くの関係者を巻き込んで形にし切る経験は、プロセス改善の専門家としてだけでなく、将来事業やチームを率いるリーダーとしての成長にも直結します。 加えて本ポジションでは、海外の関係者との連携を通じて、先進的な業界動向、多様性のある考え方、改善のアプローチ手法、そして人的ネットワークを体得できる点も魅力です。各プロジェクトを通じて日本各地の拠点のメンバーと協業し、実際の倉庫内オペレーションや配送業務を観察することで、地域のお客様へのカスタマーエクスペリエンス向上を身近に感じることができます 関連情報 The Amazon Customer Excellence System (ACES) team is hiring a Process Improvement Manager to drive process improvement across our operations end to end, from first mile through last mile. **Role and responsibilities** The ACES team improves the safety, quality, and productivity of in-building operations end to end, from first mile sites such as fulfillment centers and sort centers through last mile sites such as delivery stations, building the mechanisms that ensure customers receive their orders when they need them and thereby elevating the customer experience. To raise the efficiency of in-building operations, we drive the introduction of new systems and mechanisms as well as improvement projects. We adapt systems and mechanisms newly deployed elsewhere in Amazon's global network to sites in Japan, lead their rollout, and then validate and refine them through both data analysis and on-site observation. With an end-to-end understanding of in-building operations, we identify the items that raise safety, quality, and productivity and drive improvement. We quantify waste from operational data and on-site observation, set priorities, and run improvement cycles. We standardize solutions with scalability in mind so they can be applied at every site, and scale them across the network. You will deliver this work in partnership with site leaders and stakeholders across the business. We are looking for candidates who, in any industry, have taken the initiative to solve business process problems themselves. Specifically, experience not only analyzing data extracted from systems to identify problems, but also driving countermeasures and improvements based on facts gathered on site, leading the work while engaging many stakeholders. Our team includes members from manufacturing, consulting, and other backgrounds in addition to logistics. Approximately half of your working days will involve on-site work, including business travel. **Team introduction** The ACES team is a group of specialists in process design and improvement. We use data analysis and Lean methods to identify the root causes of problems and deliver fundamental improvement by changing the design of the process itself. Our scope extends beyond front-line task improvement to every factor that drives the performance of in-building operations, including inbound planning, labor planning, shift design, and associate deployment. Through best-practice sharing across sites and standardization, we support the continuous development of the entire network. A defining characteristic of ACES is that we do not confine ourselves to our own remit. To ensure Amazon's business and operations improve continuously from first mile through last mile, we engage proactively with challenges across the business, building cross-functional mechanisms to drive improvement. Where the situation or business need calls for it, we lead projects ourselves even when another organization is the nominal owner, in order to accelerate problem solving. The team consists of three sub-teams with distinct roles: **Productivity team** The Productivity team leads improvement of TPH (Throughput per Hour, the productivity metric for units processed per hour) across the end-to-end in-building flow, from labor planning through inbound, sortation, loading, and dispatch. Through data analysis and on-site observation, the team quantitatively identifies the key levers and processes that drive productivity and delivers durable improvement. It supports sites whose performance is lagging, extracts best practices from top-performing sites and scales them across the network, and achieves fundamental improvement by changing the mechanism of the process itself. Drawing on deep process knowledge, the team also develops and provides the deep-dive tools operations teams use for day-to-day improvement, dynamically reprioritizing toward the areas with the largest impact and moving with a strong bias for action. **PI team** The PI (Process Improvement) team is a group of experts in in-building operational processes who deliver continuous productivity gains and sustainable growth across the Japan Operations network through data-driven analysis and process optimization, grounded in going to the actual place to see the actual thing. The team leads or supports every cross-functional initiative spanning first mile through last mile operations, providing deep process expertise, quantitative evaluation using Lean methods, and optimal process design and standardization that eliminates overburden, unevenness, and waste. Even for initiatives owned by other organizations, the team takes a network-wide view to judge where course correction is needed and leads the work when necessary. It provides the support operations need for standards to take hold, and owns delivery through to network-wide rollout. The team also maintains an integrated view of every initiative affecting our processes, builds short-, mid-, and long-term productivity plans, and secures alignment with business leadership to create the strategic roadmap that underpins sustainable growth. **Lean excellence team** The Lean excellence team brings Lean Six Sigma expertise. Members statistically analyze waste and variation in processes and execute improvement through DMAIC (Define, Measure, Analyze, Improve, Control). jobs.description: AWS Applied AI Solutions (AAIS) is building toward a future where every business innovates with Amazon AI teammates. To get there, we build AI solutions that improve human capabilities and transform entire business functions. We create end-to-end products that surprise and delight out-of-the-box, making complex things easy and hard things possible, with no cloud experience required. We start with customers who embrace the future and build bridges to meet the rest where they are. We pursue ambitious opportunities with conviction, and we are looking for builders who share that mindset. Amazon WorkSpaces has protected and empowered enterprise work for over a decade and we are now reimagining what a workspace is. We are building Agentic WorkSpaces: a platform where the workspace itself is an active partner in how you work, not just infrastructure that delivers applications. Today more than a million users rely on WorkSpaces daily; tomorrow those workspaces will host AI agents alongside humans — agents that code, troubleshoot, analyze, and act on behalf of their users, governed by the same identity and security policies as the people they serve. We compete with Microsoft, Citrix, and Omnissa, and we intend to leapfrog them by building the workspace that was designed for the agentic era, not retrofitted for it. Agentic Workspaces' On-Instance Software (OIS) is the layer that makes this possible from the inside of every WorkSpace: the operating-system provisioning logic, on-instance agents, telemetry, and update mechanisms across Windows and Linux. Our vision is for that software to be invisible — operating systems that launch within weeks of upstream general availability, agents that update themselves safely without disrupting access, provisioning that is self-diagnosable, and fleet management that works through the same AWS tools customers already use — delivered from commercial regions to classified partitions with automation as the default, so quality and breadth improve release over release. Knowledge of Linux operating systems, Linux package management, and native Linux desktop application development is desired. You want to solve challenging problems in operating systems, identity, AI, and desktop platform engineering at a scale that impacts more than a million users daily. We are looking for a Software Development Engineer to design, build, and operate the services and agents that provision, secure, and maintain WorkSpaces for humans and increasingly for the AI agents that work beside them across every supported OS and identity provider. As a developer on our team, you'll own code end-to-end from design to development and work closely with senior technical leaders within the team and across AWS. You will own end-to-end delivery of features and systems within OIS - from design through deployment and operations - holding a high bar for availability, latency, and security. You are customer-obsessed, technically deep, and energized by solving hard problems. You think big about what the workspace of the future looks like — a unified agent shipping to two platforms from one code base, an identity model that treats humans and agents as first-class citizens, and autonomous troubleshooting that resolves issues before users notice — and then you build the systems to get there. Key job responsibilities • Design and deliver features and systems within On-Instance Software, contributing to the architecture strategy for how the on-instance layer evolves to host and govern AI agents alongside human users. • Drive the agent unification work that lets Windows and Linux features ship from a single codebase, making feature parity the default rather than a follow-up. Partner with EC2, identity providers, self-service troubleshooting, and platform teams — earning trust by driving technical discussions that result in impactful architectural decisions. • Design and implement on-instance identity, security, and governance for a world where humans and agents share the same desktop: identity integration across the major identity join models, a trust and authorization posture that treats agents as first-class principals, and compliance-ready images built in rather than bolted on. • Own the operation of low-latency, high-availability provisioning and agent services used by more than one million WorkSpaces users globally. Ensure your services meet stringent SLAs across multiple production regions, AWS partitions, and OS variants with self-service diagnostics and autonomous issue resolution before customers are impacted. • Drive engineering excellence through instrumentation, automated testing, and pipeline-based deployment — eliminating manual toil and shipping features simultaneously across Windows and Linux. Think big about the agentic era and experiment boldly with AI-powered capabilities such as conversational setup, natural-language troubleshooting, and AI-assisted fleet management. • Raise the bar on customer self-service so operating-system breadth, safe automatic updates, and reliable provisioning are delivered without imposing an operational tax on the customer or the agent workflows running on the desktop. About the team Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn't followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don't let it stop you from applying. Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world's most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that's why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses. We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why flexible work hours and arrangements are part of our culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there's nothing we can't achieve in the cloud. Here at AWS, it's in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity and AmazeCon conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness. We're continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth's Best Employer. That's why you'll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

We are looking for a Senior Technical Program Manager (TPM) to lead the development and deployment of Avionics Test Systems that enable the test, validation, and scaled production of Leo satellite sub-systems. This is a high-impact role where your work will directly influence how quickly and reliably we deploy satellites to orbit.

As a Senior TPM for Avionics Test Systems, you will own the end-to-end technical program strategy for the test equipment, automation, and infrastructure required to verify Avionics Line Replaceable Units (LRUs) across their lifecycle—from engineering development through production-rate testing.

You will partner with cross-functional teams across test engineering, electrical design, embedded software, manufacturing, and external vendors to develop and deploy test systems that meet the demanding requirements of space-grade hardware validation.

This role sits at the intersection of test engineering, hardware-software integration, vendor management, and production scale-up. Success requires deep technical judgment in test system architecture, strong program leadership across internal and external development teams, and the ability to drive alignment between product development timelines and test readiness milestones.

Key job responsibilities
Help Build the Infrastructure That Connects the World:
The programs you lead will become core components of Amazon’s satellite network, enabling reliable broadband connectivity for communities around the globe. Your work will help bring high-speed internet access to millions of people who currently lack it, expanding access to education, healthcare, and economic opportunity.

Lead Avionics Test System Development End-to-End:
Own the technical program strategy for test systems that validate avionics LRUs—from requirements definition and architecture through design, integration, commissioning, and production deployment. Define verification and validation strategies that demonstrate sub-system performance and flight readiness at scale.

Drive Test System Readiness Across Internal and Vendor Teams:
Serve as the central program leader coordinating test system development across internal test engineering teams and external vendors. Ensure test stations are designed, built, qualified, and delivered on schedule to support production milestones and new product introduction timelines.

Own Test Architecture Decisions and Trade Studies:
Drive trade studies with engineering that balance test coverage, throughput, cost, and maintainability. Define test system requirements that align with LRU design evolution across program workstreams while managing interfaces between test systems and flight hardware.

Scale Test Infrastructure for High-Rate Production:
Transition test systems from engineering development environments into production-rate capable stations supporting one of the largest satellite constellations ever built. Drive test automation, reliability improvements, and capacity planning to meet factory throughput targets.
